mainTopic: Harsh language about ערי מקלט and disputes of רבי יהודה; which כהן גדול's death frees the killer; the power of prayer and of a חכם's curse
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about why the section on ערי מקלט in ספר יהושע uses the harsh word דיבור. It answers that the cities are a מצוה of the תורה, then shows that דבר is harsh while ידבר is gentle. After a סימן, it lists three disputes involving רבי יהודה without saying who holds which view: the reason for the harsh language, what יהושע wrote 'in the scroll of the תורה,' and whether a ספר תורה sewn with linen is כשר. רב reports seeing תפילין sewn with linen, but the הלכה requires sinews. A new משנה lists which kinds of כהן גדול free the accidental killer when they die, and רבי יהודה adds the משוח מלחמה. The משנה also says the mothers of the כהנים fed and clothed the exiles so they would not pray for their sons' death. The גמרא learns the kinds of כהן גדול from the פסוקים and explains that a prayer against the כהן גדול can work, because he should have prayed for his generation. It closes with two teachings: a חכם's curse comes true even when it is baseless (דוד and אחיתופל) and even when it is conditional (עלי and שמואל).

steps.title: Why is the section about ערי מקלט in harsh language?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes asking why the פרשה of ערי מקלט in ספר יהושע is said with the harsh word for speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is this section written in harsh language? As it says: 'And ה׳ spoke to יהושע, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, saying: Assign for yourselves the cities of refuge that I spoke to you about.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that started on the previous page: why does this פסוק about ערי מקלט use the strong, harsh word for speaking? It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hebrew has two common words for speaking. אמירה is neutral, and דיבור is stronger and harsher. This פסוק uses forms of דיבור three times (וידבר, דבר, דברתי), so the גמרא wants to know why the language is so forceful here.

keyTerms.meaning: Harsh, forceful language
Cities of refuge, where someone who killed by accident could run to
'And He spoke,' a form of דיבור, the stronger word for speaking

steps.confusionAlert: This page starts in the middle of a sentence. The question 'Why was this section said…' began on the previous page, and here we only see its end.

phrases.english: in harsh language,
phrases.notes: This finishes a question from the previous page: why was this section said in harsh language?

phrases.english: as it is written:
"And the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying:
phrases.notes: יהושע 20:1–2

phrases.english: Speak to the children of Israel, saying:
Assign for yourselves the cities of refuge
of which I spoke to you, etc."?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question begun at the end of the previous page
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק about ערי מקלט repeatedly uses the harsh word דיבור

steps.title: Because ערי מקלט are a מצוה of the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the language is harsh because ערי מקלט are a מצוה from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are a commandment of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the strong language is used because ערי מקלט are a מצוה written in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this is a תורה commandment and not a minor matter, ה׳ speaks forcefully to stress how important it is. The harsh tone signals seriousness, not anger.

keyTerms.meaning: From the תורה; a commandment written in the תורה itself
Because

phrases.english: Because they are of the Torah.
phrases.notes: He means the cities of refuge are a מצוה commanded in the תורה, so the command is stressed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The harsh language stresses that ערי מקלט are a תורה commandment

steps.title: Does every form of 'speaking' mean harsh speech?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the answer means that every use of דיבור signals harsh language.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that every time the word דיבור is used, it is harsh language?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the assumption behind the last step. Is every form of the word דיבור harsh?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 2 only works if the word דיבור itself signals harshness. So the גמרא asks whether this is a general rule about the word everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say…? It introduces a question about what follows from an idea
Speaking; the stronger word for speech
Hard, harsh language

phrases.english: Is that to say that every 'speaking' is harsh language?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption behind the answer of step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether דיבור always means harsh speech

steps.title: Yes — proof from יוסף speaking harshly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says yes, and proves it from the brothers' report that 'the man spoke (דבר) harshly to us.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as it says: 'The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly with us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes, דיבור is harsh speech. It brings a פסוק where the brothers describe יוסף speaking roughly to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק the word דבר appears right next to קשות (harsh things). That shows the word fits harsh speech.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Harsh things, harshly

phrases.english: Yes, as it is written:
"The man, the lord of the land, spoke
phrases.notes: בראשית 42:30. The brothers are describing יוסף, who was ruling מצרים.

phrases.english: harshly with us."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 with a proof from a פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, דיבור is harsh speech, as seen in בראשית 42:30

steps.title: A ברייתא says this word means gentle speech
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from a ברייתא that calls נדברו and ידבר gentle words.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: the word 'נדברו' is only gentle language. And it also says, 'He will lead (ידבר) nations under us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule that דיבור is always harsh. It quotes a ברייתא saying that forms of this same root mean gentle speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נדברו and ידבר come from the same root as דבר. If they are gentle, then the root by itself cannot mean harshness, and the rule from step 4 seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They spoke with one another (מלאכי 3:16)
Gentle, calm language
He will lead or subdue, gently (תהלים 47:4)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: "They spoke [nidberu],"
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:16

phrases.english: "they spoke" is nothing other than gentle language,
and so too it says:
"He leads [yadber] peoples under us"!
phrases.notes: תהלים 47:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that every דיבור is harsh speech
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא treats forms of the same root (נדברו, ידבר) as gentle, so the root cannot always mean harsh

steps.title: Different forms of the word mean different things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that דבר and ידבר are separate forms with separate meanings.
steps.simpleTranslation: דבר is one thing, and ידבר is another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. Even though the words share a root, the form דבר means harsh speech and the form ידבר means gentle leading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'דיבור is harsh' applies to the form used in our פסוקים (דבר, וידבר). The ברייתא was talking about different forms, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Separately; a thing of its own
He spoke, the form that means harsh speech

steps.whatToRemember: The word form matters. דבר/וידבר means harsh speech, while ידבר/נדברו can mean gentle speech, even though they share a root.

phrases.english: "Dibber" is separate, and "yadber" is separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same root must carry the same meaning in all its forms
steps.terutzMaskana: Each form has its own meaning: דבר is harsh, ידבר is gentle

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming disputes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a short memory aid (סימן) for a list of disputes involving רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: רבנן, מהמני, and ספרי.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is not an argument. It is a short memory aid, like a table of contents, to help remember a coming series of disputes involving רבי יהודה. It prepares the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one dispute. 'רבנן' is the dispute with the רבנן that comes right next, 'מהמני' is a dispute with רבי נחמיה, and 'ספרי' is a dispute about ספרי תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Memory aids, key words to help remember a sequence
Key word pointing to the dispute with רבי נחמיה
Scrolls; key word pointing to the dispute about ספרי תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to translate this line as a sentence. It is just a list of key words to help remember what comes next.

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: Rabbis, mehemni, and scrolls).
phrases.notes: These are just memory hooks for the next few disputes involving רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A short break before returning to the topic of harsh language
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory aid for the disputes of רבי יהודה that follow

steps.title: רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree about the reason for harsh language
steps.stepSummary: One opinion says the harsh language was because they delayed setting up the cities. The other says it was because the cities are a תורה commandment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree about this. One says: because they delayed. The other says: because they are a commandment of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the question of why harsh language is used about ערי מקלט and reports a dispute. One opinion gives a new reason, the delay. The other gives the reason we already saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second opinion is the same answer as step 2. The first opinion adds something new: the harshness was a scolding because the setting up of the cities was delayed. The גמרא does not say which sage holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
They delayed
One says (without naming which sage)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for the harsh language about ערי מקלט: (1) a scolding for the delay in setting them up, or (2) stressing that they are a תורה commandment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis disagree about this:
One says: because they delayed it.
phrases.notes: He means the delay in setting aside the cities of refuge, so the harsh tone is a kind of scolding.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אוֹמֵר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: And one says: because they are of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question of steps 1–2 and presents it as a dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: the harsh language is either because of the delay or because the cities are a תורה commandment

steps.title: What did יהושע write in the scroll of the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה argue about the פסוק 'And יהושע wrote these matters in the scroll of the Torah of God.' One says it means the last eight פסוקים of the תורה. The other says it means the section about ערי מקלט.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And יהושע wrote these matters in the scroll of the תורה of God." רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה disagree about this. One says: it means the eight פסוקים. The other says: it means ערי מקלט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another dispute from the list in the סימן. Two sages argue about what יהושע wrote, and we don't know who holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says יהושע wrote 'these matters' in the תורה scroll. One view says this means the last eight פסוקים of the תורה, which tell about משה's death. The other view says it means the ערי מקלט section in ספר יהושע, which ties this dispute to our topic.

keyTerms.meaning: Cities of refuge, where someone who killed by accident can run to
Eight verses, meaning the last eight פסוקים of the תורה
They disagree about it
One says... and one says. We are not told which sage holds which view

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to match each opinion to a name. The point of this list (from the סימן) is that we don't know which sage said which view.

phrases.english: "And Joshua wrote these matters
in the scroll of the Torah of God"
phrases.notes: יהושע 24:26

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya disagree about it
One says: the eight verses
phrases.notes: These are the last eight פסוקים of the תורה, which tell about משה's death.

phrases.english: and one says: the cities of refuge.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item on the list of unattributed disputes introduced by the סימן in step 7, linked to ערי מקלט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'matters' יהושע wrote are either the last eight פסוקים of the תורה or the ערי מקלט section.

steps.title: How does the ערי מקלט view fit the words 'scroll of the תורה'?
steps.stepSummary: The eight-פסוקים view fits the words 'in the scroll of the Torah of God,' since those פסוקים are in the תורה. But the ערי מקלט section is in ספר יהושע, so how does that view explain those words?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who says eight פסוקים; that is why it is written "in the scroll of the תורה of God." But according to the one who says ערי מקלט, what does "in the scroll of the תורה of God" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ערי מקלט view, because the פסוק says יהושע wrote in the תורה scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eight פסוקים really are inside the תורה, so that view matches the words of the פסוק. The ערי מקלט section is in ספר יהושע, not in the תורה. So the words 'scroll of the Torah of God' seem to contradict this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this makes sense. Opens a contrast between two views
But. Brings the side that has a problem
What? Here it means 'how do you explain...?'

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says eight verses,
that is why it is written: "in the scroll of the Torah of God."
But according to the one who says cities of refuge,
what is "in the scroll of the Torah of God"?
phrases.notes: The ערי מקלט section is in ספר יהושע, not in the תורה, so the words seem not to fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both views from step 9 against the wording of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the פסוק refers to ערי מקלט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'in the scroll of the Torah of God,' but the ערי מקלט section is in ספר יהושע, not in the תורה.

steps.title: Rereading the פסוק: יהושע wrote in his own book
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the פסוק: יהושע wrote, in his own book, the matters that are already written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: "And יהושע wrote in his book these matters that are written in the scroll of the תורה of God."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the פסוק a different way. The words 'scroll of the תורה' describe where the matters come from, not where יהושע wrote them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in the scroll of the Torah of God' now describe the matters themselves: these laws are already found in the תורה. יהושע wrote them in his own book. Since ערי מקלט do appear in the תורה, the ערי מקלט view now fits the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Introduces a new reading of a text
In his own book, meaning ספר יהושע

steps.whatToRemember: Both views can stand. 'In the scroll of the תורה' can mean the place יהושע wrote, or the source of what he wrote.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
"And Joshua wrote in his book
phrases.notes: This is not an exact quote. The גמרא is rewording the פסוק to show how this view reads it.

phrases.english: these matters
that are written in the scroll of the Torah of God."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In the scroll of the Torah' tells us where יהושע wrote, so it must mean the תורה itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In the scroll of the Torah' describes the matters, which already appear in the תורה; יהושע wrote them in his own book.

steps.title: A ספר תורה sewn with linen thread
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר argue about a ספר תורה whose sheets were sewn together with linen thread. One says it is כשר, the other says it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ספר תורה that one sewed with linen: רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר disagree about it. One says it is כשר; the other says it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next dispute from the סימן list. It is about sewing a ספר תורה with linen instead of animal sinews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sheets of a ספר תורה are sewn together. The question is whether linen thread is acceptable. As before, we are not told which sage holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: Linen (flax) thread
Fit, kosher for use
Unfit, may not be used
Sewed (the sheets together)

phrases.english: A Torah scroll that one sewed with linen,

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir disagree about it:
one says: it is fit,
and one says: it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the list of unattributed disputes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute whether a ספר תורה sewn with linen is כשר or פסול.

steps.title: Why linen is פסול: the תורה is compared to תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The פסול view learns from a פסוק about תפילין that the whole תורה is compared to תפילין. תפילין must be sewn with sinews (הלכה למשה מסיני), so a ספר תורה must be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says פסול: it is written, "so that the תורה of ה׳ will be in your mouth," and the entire תורה is compared to תפילין. Just as תפילין have a law given to משה at סיני that they be sewn with sinews, so too every ספר תורה must be sewn with sinews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the view that linen is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about תפילין mentions 'the Torah of ה׳,' which links the whole תורה to תפילין in a הקש. There is a הלכה למשה מסיני that תפילין are sewn with sinews. Through the הקש, a ספר תורה needs sinews too, so linen is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is compared (by a הֶקֵּשׁ, a link the פסוק makes between two topics)
A law given orally to משה at סיני
Sinews (animal tendons) used as thread
Tefillin, worn on the arm and head

phrases.english: According to the one who says unfit,
it is because it is written: "so that the Torah of ה׳ will be in your mouth,"
phrases.notes: שמות 13:9. This פסוק is about תפילין.

phrases.english: and the entire Torah is compared to tefillin:
just as for tefillin there is a law given to Moshe at Sinai
to sew them with sinews,
so too all must be sewn with sinews.
phrases.notes: 'All' means every ספר תורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the פסול view from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the הקש compares a ספר תורה to תפילין, it must be sewn with sinews, so linen is פסול.

steps.title: The other view: the comparison covers only kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: The כשר view says the הקש to תפילין only teaches that a ספר תורה must be made from an animal that is permitted to eat. It does not teach the other laws of תפילין, like sewing with sinews.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other sage? When the תורה is compared to תפילין, it is only about what is permitted in your mouth. For its other laws, it is not compared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the כשר view answers the הקש. It limits the comparison to one law only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in your mouth' point to food. So the הקש only teaches that, like תפילין, a ספר תורה must be written on the skin of a kosher animal. It does not teach the sewing law, so linen is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? Asks how the other view handles the argument
What is permitted in your mouth, meaning kosher animals
Its other laws (of תפילין)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides accept the הקש between the תורה and תפילין. They argue about how far it reaches: all the laws of תפילין, or only the kosher-animal rule.

phrases.english: And the other sage?
When it is compared, it is about what is permitted in your mouth,
phrases.notes: The skin must come from an animal a Jew is allowed to eat.

phrases.english: but for its other laws, it is not compared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of step 13 from the point of view of the כשר opinion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the הקש rather than rejecting it entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסול view stretches the הקש to all laws of תפילין, but 'in your mouth' only points to the kosher-animal rule.

steps.title: רב saw תפילין sewn with linen, but the הלכה is not like that
steps.stepSummary: רב reports that the תפילין in his uncle's house were sewn with linen. The גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: I saw the תפילין of my uncle's house, and they were sewn with linen. But the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells us he saw real תפילין sewn with linen thread, not sinews. Right after, the גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow this practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps argued about whether a ספר תורה may be sewn with linen, based on comparing it to תפילין. רב's report shows that someone allowed linen even for תפילין themselves. The ruling at the end shuts that down: תפילין must be sewn with sinews.

keyTerms.meaning: Linen (flax) thread
Sewn, stitched
The halacha is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, תפילין are sewn with sinews, not linen, even though רב saw a household that used linen.
steps.confusionAlert: רב is not giving his own ruling that linen is fine. He is reporting what he saw. The line after it is the actual ruling, and it rejects that practice.

phrases.english: Rav said:
I saw the tefillin of the house of my uncle
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא, רב's uncle.

phrases.english: that were sewn with linen.
But the halacha is not like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב חזינן להו לתפילין דבי חביבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an eyewitness report about linen-sewn תפילין, then closes the linen-thread topic with a practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילין sewn with linen were seen in practice, but the הלכה requires sinews.

steps.title: Which kinds of כהן גדול free the killer when they die
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three kinds of כהן גדול whose death sends the רוצח home. רבי יהודה adds the משוח מלחמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One anointed with the anointing oil, one who wears the many garments, and one who has left his anointed position — each of them brings the killer back home. רבי יהודה says: even the כהן anointed for war brings the killer back.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us which kinds of כהן גדול end the exile of the accidental killer when they die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the רוצח stays in the עיר מקלט until the death of the כהן גדול. The משנה says three types count: one anointed with oil, one appointed by wearing the eight special garments, and a former כהן גדול who stepped down. רבי יהודה goes further and includes the כהן anointed to speak to the army before war.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול anointed with the special anointing oil
A כהן גדול appointed by wearing the extra (eight) priestly garments
A כהן גדול who has stepped down from his position
The כהן anointed to address the army before battle
Here: someone who killed by accident and fled to an עיר מקלט

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole new topic. The גמרא will next ask where each of these types comes from in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Both one anointed with the anointing oil,
and one with the many garments,
phrases.notes: This is a כהן גדול who became כהן גדול by putting on the eight special garments, without the oil.

phrases.english: and one who has left his anointed position –
phrases.notes: This means a substitute כהן גדול who stepped down once the regular one could serve again.

phrases.english: bring the killer back.
phrases.notes: He means their death lets the killer go home from the עיר מקלט.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even the priest anointed for war
brings the killer back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new משנה. It is unrelated to the linen-thread discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The death of any of the three kinds of כהן גדול frees the רוצח. רבי יהודה adds the משוח מלחמה.

steps.title: The mothers of כהנים supplied the exiles so they would not pray for their sons' death
steps.stepSummary: Because the exiles wait for the כהן גדול to die, the כהנים' mothers gave them food and clothing so they would not pray for that death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, the mothers of the priests would provide them with food and clothing, so that they would not pray that their sons die.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a practical result of the rule we just learned. The exiles go free when the כהן גדול dies, so the כהנים' mothers kept the exiles comfortable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exile ends only with the כהן גדול's death, so an exile might wish for it. The mothers gave the exiles food and clothing. That way the exiles would be content and would not pray for the death of the mothers' sons.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore — introduces a result of the rule just stated
Food and clothing
They provide, supply

phrases.english: Therefore, the mothers of the priests
provide them with food and clothing,
phrases.notes: "Them" here means the exiles living in the עיר מקלט.

phrases.english: so that they will not pray
about their sons, that they should die.

steps.triggerLanguage: לפיכך אימותיהן של כהנים מספקות להן מחיה וכסות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical outcome from the rule that the כהן גדול's death frees the exile.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים' mothers supplied the exiles with food and clothing so they would not pray for the כהנים' death.

steps.title: Where do we learn these three kinds of כהן גדול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that all three kinds of כהן גדול free the killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's list. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that three different kinds of כהן גדול all count. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that each of them frees the רוצח.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? — a request for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the משנה's list in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that all three kinds of כהן גדול end the exile.

steps.title: Three פסוקים mention the death of the כהן גדול, one for each kind
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings three phrases from the תורה that each mention the death of the כהן גדול. These match the three kinds in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The verse says, "And he shall dwell there until the death of the High Priest," and it is written, "For in his city of refuge he shall dwell until the death of the High Priest," and it is written, "And after the death of the High Priest."
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question. He points to three places where the פסוקים mention the death of the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have mentioned the death of the כהן גדול just once. Because it mentions it three times, each mention teaches one more kind of כהן גדול: one anointed with oil, one appointed with the garments, and one who stepped down.

keyTerms.meaning: As the verse says
City of refuge, where the accidental killer lives in exile
The High Priest

steps.whatToRemember: Three mentions of "the death of the כהן גדול" in the פסוקים give us three kinds of כהן גדול whose death sends the רוצח home.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
As the verse says:
"And he shall dwell in it
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:25

phrases.english: until the death of the High Priest,"
and it is written: "For in his city of refuge he shall dwell
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:28

phrases.english: until the death of the High Priest,"
and it is written: "And after the death of the High Priest."
phrases.notes: Also from במדבר 35:28. That makes three mentions in all, one for each kind of כהן גדול in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18 with three פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The death of the כהן גדול is mentioned three times in the פסוקים. Each mention matches one of the three kinds listed in the משנה.

steps.title: The verse רבי יהודה uses for the משוח מלחמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns that the משוח מלחמה also frees the killer. It answers that he uses a fourth verse that mentions the death of 'the priest.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about רבי יהודה, who adds a fourth kind? Another verse is written: 'To return to live in the land until the death of the priest.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא found three verses for the three kinds of כהן גדול. Now the גמרא asks where רבי יהודה gets a fourth kind, the משוח מלחמה, and points to another verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three earlier verses match the three kinds in the משנה. רבי יהודה adds a fourth kind, so he needs a fourth verse. He finds it in במדבר 35:32, which talks about the death of 'the priest.'

keyTerms.meaning: Another verse
The כהן anointed to lead the people in war
The death of the priest

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה?
phrases.notes: He means: where does רבי יהודה get his fourth kind, the משוח מלחמה?

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
"To return to live in the land
until the death of the priest." (and so on)
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:32. Some versions have the round-bracket word 'and so on' and some don't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב כהנא's three-verse source to explain רבי יהודה's fourth kind.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does רבי יהודה learn that the משוח מלחמה also frees the killer?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From an extra verse, 'until the death of the priest' (במדבר 35:32).

steps.title: How the other view reads that same verse
steps.stepSummary: The other תנא says the verse does not say 'the great' priest, so it is not a new kind. It just refers to one of the three kinds already mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view? Since the verse does not write 'the great,' it is talking about one of those same kinds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other view does not learn a fourth kind from רבי יהודה's verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other three verses call him the 'great' priest (כהן גדול). This verse only says 'the priest.' So the other view reads it as pointing back to one of the כהנים already listed, not as adding the משוח מלחמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one; here, the תנא who disagrees with רבי יהודה
'The great,' the word that marks a כהן גדול
One of those (already mentioned)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns a fourth kind of כהן from 'until the death of the priest.' The other view says that verse has no word 'great,' so it just repeats one of the three kinds.

phrases.english: And the other one?
Since "the great" is not written,
it is one of those.
phrases.notes: One of the three kinds of כהן גדול already learned from the earlier verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other view's reading of the verse רבי יהודה used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why doesn't the other view learn a fourth kind from this verse?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse lacks 'the great,' so it refers back to one of the three kinds already listed.

steps.title: Can a prayer against an innocent כהן גדול work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the mothers of the כהנים. It reads it as saying that if the exiles prayed for the כהן גדול to die, he really might die. It then challenges this from a פסוק: a curse with no reason does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Therefore the mothers of the כהנים...' This means the reason he does not die is that the exiles don't pray. So if they did pray, he would die? But it is written: 'Like a sparrow wandering, like a swallow flying, so a baseless curse will not come about'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the line in the משנה about the mothers. It challenges the idea that a curse against an innocent כהן גדול could work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mothers gave gifts so the exiles would not pray for their sons' deaths. That suggests such a prayer could really kill him. But the כהן גדול did nothing to the killer, and משלי says a baseless curse has no power. So why worry?

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
They pray
They die
A curse for no reason, a baseless curse

phrases.english: "Therefore the mothers of the כהנים..." etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the line of the משנה we saw in step 17.

phrases.english: The reason is that they don't pray,
but if they did pray, they would die?
But isn't it written: "Like a sparrow wandering, like a swallow flying,
so a baseless curse will not come about"!
phrases.notes: משלי 26:2

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלָא מְצַלּוּ, הָא מְצַלּוּ מָיְיתִי? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources for the כהן גדול to the line in the משנה about the mothers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implication that a prayer for the כהן גדול's death could work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן גדול did nothing wrong, and משלי teaches that a baseless curse does not take effect.

steps.title: The curse is not baseless: they should have prayed
steps.stepSummary: An elder quotes רבא's lecture: the כהנים גדולים should have prayed for mercy for their generation and did not. So they share some blame, and the curse has a reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said: I heard in רבא's lecture that they should have asked for mercy for their generation, and they did not ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The curse is not 'for no reason,' because the כהן גדול did fail in something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the כהן גדול was fully innocent. The answer says he had a duty to pray that such deaths would not happen in his generation. Since he did not pray, he carries some blame, so a prayer against him can take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A public lecture given by a sage
To ask for mercy, to pray
Their generation

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a leader is partly responsible for what happens in his generation if he did not pray for it.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him:
I heard from רבא's lecture:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶן לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל דּוֹרָן
phrases.english: that they should have asked for mercy for their generation
and they did not ask.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the כהנים גדולים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא: מִפִּירְקֵיהּ דְּרָבָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from 'a baseless curse.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenge's assumption that the כהן גדול is fully innocent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן גדול did nothing wrong, so a curse against him would have no power.
steps.terutzMaskana: He failed to pray for his generation, so the curse has a reason and can work.

steps.title: A second version: the exiles pray for the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: Some teach the משנה differently. The mothers gave gifts so the exiles would pray that their sons would NOT die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it this way: so that they will pray for their sons, that they should not die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the משנה's wording. This sets up a new question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the gifts stop the exiles from praying against the כהן גדול. In this version, the gifts get the exiles to pray in his favor. The wording changes, and the next step asks a question based on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (this way); a different version
That they will pray

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. Version one: the gifts stop the exiles from praying for his death. Version two: the gifts get them to pray for his life.

phrases.english: And some teach:
so that they will pray for their sons
that they should not die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the same line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version the mothers' gifts were meant to get the exiles to pray that the כהנים would not die.

steps.title: What could the כהן גדול have done?
steps.stepSummary: From the second version, the גמרא infers that without the exiles' prayers the כהן גדול would die. It asks why he deserves this, since he had nothing to do with the killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he lives is that they pray. So if they did not pray, he would die? What should he have done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version. It asks why the כהן גדול should be in danger of death for someone else's killing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version implies the כהן גדול needs the exiles' prayers to stay alive. That means he is already under some punishment. But the killing was done by someone else, so the גמרא asks what he could have done to stop it.

keyTerms.meaning: What should he have done? (He had no way to prevent it)

phrases.english: The reason is that they pray,
but if they did not pray, they would die?
What should he have done?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן גדול. The killing happened without him.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּמְצַלּוּ, הָא לָא מְצַלּוּ מָיְיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the second version and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of the second version that the כהן גדול would die without the exiles' prayers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן גדול had no part in the killing, so it seems unfair that he would be in danger.

steps.title: Two sayings about suffering for someone else's sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens its question with two folk sayings. In בבל they say: Toviyya sinned and Zigud gets lashes. In ארץ ישראל they say: Shechem marries and Mavgai gets circumcised.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we say: 'Toviyya sinned and Zigud gets lashes.' There they say: 'Shechem marries and Mavgai gets circumcised.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two well-known sayings to show how unfair the situation looks. They are part of the challenge from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each saying describes one person who does something while another person pays the price. This is just how it looks when the killer sins and the כהן גדול is the one in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (בבל) / there (ארץ ישראל)
Gets lashes
Marries
Gets circumcised

steps.whatToRemember: The second version of the משנה raises a strong question: why should the כהן גדול suffer for the killer's act? The two sayings describe exactly this kind of unfairness.

phrases.english: Here we say:
phrases.notes: 'Here' means בבל.

phrases.english: Toviyya sinned and Zigud gets lashes.
phrases.notes: Zigud came alone to testify against Toviyya. A lone witness is not accepted, so Zigud was the one punished.

phrases.english: There they say:
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Shechem marries and Mavgai gets circumcised.
phrases.notes: See בראשית 34. Shechem married דינה, and the other men of the city had to be circumcised.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא אָמְרִינַן: טוֹבִיָּה חֲטָא וְזִיגּוּד מִנַּגַּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the previous challenge with two sayings about one person paying for another's act.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two folk sayings show the unfairness of one person suffering for another's sin, which sharpens the question about the כהן גדול.

steps.title: The elder's answer: the כהנים גדולים failed to pray for their generation
steps.stepSummary: An elder quotes רבא's lecture: the כהנים גדולים should have asked for mercy for their generation and did not, so they share some of the blame.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said: I heard in רבא's lecture that they should have asked for mercy for their generation, and they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: An old man answers the question from steps 25 and 26 about why the כהן גדול should suffer for a killing he did not do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the כהן גדול had nothing to do with the killing. The answer says he did have a part: a leader is supposed to pray that such disasters don't happen, and he did not pray. So he is not 'Zigud getting lashes for Toviyya'. He carries some real blame.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder, an old man
His public lecture (a lesson given to the public)
To ask for mercy, to pray for others
Their generation

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him:
I heard from the lecture of Rava,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶן לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל דּוֹרָן
phrases.english: that they should have asked for mercy for their generation
phrases.notes: 'They' means the כהנים גדולים.

phrases.english: and they did not ask.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא: מִפִּירְקֵיהּ דְּרָבָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sharpened question of step 26 (Toviyya sinned and Zigud is punished).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the punished person is actually partly at fault
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן גדול is completely innocent of the killing, so punishing him is unfair.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן גדול failed in his duty to pray for his generation, so he shares the blame.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי and the man eaten by a lion
steps.stepSummary: A story shows that a leader is held responsible for disasters near him: אליהו stopped speaking with רבי יהושע בן לוי for three days after a man was killed by a lion near his town.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of a man who was eaten by a lion three parasangs away from רבי יהושע בן לוי, and אליהו did not speak with him for three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the elder's idea with a story about a great leader who was held responsible for a death near his town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי did not cause the lion attack, and it happened some distance from him. Still, אליהו held back from him, which shows a leader is expected to pray that such things don't happen in his area. This is the same reasoning as the blame on the כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: A lion
Parasangs, a measure of distance (a few kilometers each)
Spoke, talked

phrases.english: Like this case of a certain man
who was eaten by a lion
at a distance of three parasangs
from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אִישְׁתַּעִי אֵלִיָּהוּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ תְּלָתָא יוֹמֵי.
phrases.english: and Eliyahu did not speak with him for three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַכְלֵיהּ אַרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the elder's principle with a story.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a spiritual leader is responsible for disasters he could have prayed to prevent
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי יהושע בן לוי and אליהו

steps.title: A חכם's curse comes true even without a real reason
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב teaches that a חכם's curse takes effect even when it was said for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The curse of a חכם comes true even if it was said for no reason.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא was just talking about curses that come true, it brings a new teaching about a חכם's curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 22) the גמרא said a curse with no reason does not take effect. רב adds an exception: when a חכם curses, the curse can take effect even if the person did nothing to deserve it. This is a special rule about a חכם's words, not a change to the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The curse of a sage
For nothing, without a real cause

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the rule from step 22 that a curse without a reason has no effect. It is a special exception for a חכם's curse.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The curse of a sage —
even if it is for nothing, it comes true.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: קִלְלַת חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of curses that come true to a new teaching about a sage's curse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sage's curse takes effect even if it had no real basis.

steps.title: דוד's question about the rising deep, and his curse
steps.stepSummary: The proof begins. When דוד dug the שיתין (the deep pits under the מזבח), the deep waters rose. He asked whether he could throw a shard with ה׳'s Name into the water. No one answered, so he cursed anyone who knew and kept quiet.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From אחיתופל. When דוד dug the pits, the deep rose up and threatened to flood the world. דוד asked: May I write the Name on a shard and throw it into the deep so it will stay in its place? No one answered. He said: Anyone who knows the answer and does not say it shall be strangled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רב's teaching and starts telling the story that proves it. Here it sets up the curse that will matter at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד's curse has a condition: it only applies to someone who knows the answer and stays silent. Keep this condition in mind. The proof depends on the fact that אחיתופל did not stay silent.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
The deep pits under the מזבח
The deep, the waters under the earth
A clay shard
Shall be strangled

phrases.english: From where do we know this? From Achitophel,
for at the time that David dug the pits,
the deep rose up,
and it was about to flood the world.
He said: May one write the Name on a shard
phrases.notes: 'He' is דוד, and 'the Name' means ה׳'s holy Name.

phrases.english: and throw it into the deep
so that it will stay in its place?
There was no one who said anything to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: כׇּל הַיּוֹדֵעַ דָּבָר זֶה וְאֵינוֹ אוֹמְרוֹ –
phrases.english: He said: Anyone who knows this matter and does not say it —
shall be strangled by his throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for רב's teaching and begins the story that proves it.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching that a sage's curse takes effect even without cause
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of דוד, the rising deep, and אחיתופל

steps.title: אחיתופל's קל וחומר saves the world
steps.stepSummary: אחיתופל reasons with a קל וחומר from סוטה: if the תורה lets ה׳'s Name be erased to make peace between a husband and wife, surely it may be used to save the whole world. דוד throws the shard and the water goes down.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחיתופל made a קל וחומר on his own: If the תורה says that to make peace between a man and his wife, My Name written in holiness may be erased in water, then to save the whole world, all the more so! He told דוד: It is allowed. דוד wrote the Name on a shard and threw it into the deep, and the water went down and stayed in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: אחיתופל gives דוד the answer, and it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is that אחיתופל did speak up and gave the right answer. So he is not the kind of person דוד's curse was aimed at. This sets up the surprise in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a more serious one
Shall be erased in the water (in the סוטה ritual)
It is permitted
Went down

phrases.aramaic: נָשָׂא אֲחִיתוֹפֶל קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּעַצְמוֹ, אָמַר:
phrases.english: Achitophel made a kal vachomer on his own, and said:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם בֵּין אִישׁ לְאִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: If, to make peace between a man and his wife,
the Torah said:
My Name, which was written in holiness,
phrases.notes: This is the סוטה ritual: ה׳'s Name is written on a scroll and erased into the water she drinks.

phrases.english: shall be erased in the water,

phrases.aramaic: לְכׇל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: then for the entire world, is it not all the more so?
He said to him: It is permitted.
He wrote the Name on a shard,
phrases.notes: Now it is דוד who writes and throws.

phrases.english: threw it into the deep,
and it went down and stayed in its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: אחיתופל answers דוד's question, which shows he did not stay silent.
steps.raayaObject: Shows that דוד's condition for the curse was not met by אחיתופל
steps.raayaSupportSource: אחיתופל's קל וחומר from the סוטה ritual

steps.title: Even so, אחיתופל died by strangling
steps.stepSummary: Even though אחיתופל answered, the פסוק says he later strangled himself. So דוד's curse came true even though it had no basis, which proves רב's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even so it is written: "And אחיתופל saw that his advice was not followed, and he saddled the donkey, got up, went to his house, to his city, commanded his household, and strangled himself."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof with a פסוק showing that אחיתופל died exactly the way דוד's curse said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד's curse was only for someone who knew and stayed silent, and אחיתופל spoke up. Even so, he died by strangling. This proves that a חכם's curse can come true even when the condition for it never happened.

keyTerms.meaning: And even so, despite this
His advice
And he strangled himself

steps.whatToRemember: Two lessons: (1) a leader who fails to pray for his generation shares the blame for its troubles, which is why a prayer against the כהן גדול is not a 'baseless curse'; (2) a חכם's curse can come true even without a real reason, as shown by אחיתופל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how seriously חז"ל took the words of a חכם. Even a conditional curse whose condition was never met still had an effect.

phrases.english: And even so, it is written:
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 17:23

phrases.english: "And Achitophel saw that his advice was not followed
and he saddled the donkey and got up
and went to his house, to his city
phrases.notes: Some versions have the extra ו in round brackets and some don't. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: and he commanded his household and strangled himself, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof: even though אחיתופל answered, the curse still came true.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching that a sage's curse comes true even without a basis
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 17:23, which describes אחיתופל strangling himself

steps.title: A חכם's curse comes true even when it was conditional
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that a חכם's curse takes effect even when it was said only on a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says: a חכם's curse comes true even if it was said on a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אבהו, similar to רב's teaching in Step 29. A חכם's curse can take effect even when it was only conditional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a curse works even when it is baseless (על חנם). רבי אבהו adds a different case: the curse was attached to a condition, and the condition was never broken. Even then, the curse still has some effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The curse of a Sage
On a condition; said in an 'if...' form
It comes, meaning it comes true

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same as רב's teaching. רב spoke about a curse said for no reason, while רבי אבהו speaks about a curse that depended on a condition the person actually kept.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:
The curse of a Sage,
even if it was conditional, it comes true.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching to רב's statement (Step 29), which was just proven in Steps 30-32
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם's curse takes effect even when it was said on a condition and the condition was kept.

steps.title: The source: עלי's conditional curse on שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source and points to עלי, who cursed שמואל if he hid any part of the prophecy from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From עלי, who said to שמואל: 'So may God do to you, and more, if you hide anything from me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רבי אבהו's teaching and begins the proof with עלי's conditional curse. This sets up the next step, where we see what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עלי's words were an 'if' curse: the curse applies only if שמואל hides something. This gives us exactly the case רבי אבהו is talking about, a curse that depends on a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
'So may God do to you,' a form of oath or curse
You will hide or hold back

phrases.english: From where do we know this? From Eli,
as [Eli] said to Shmuel:
phrases.notes: The name in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, making clear who is speaking.

phrases.english: "So may God do to you, and more also,"
"if you hide anything from me."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 3:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for and begins the source for רבי אבהו's teaching
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's rule that a conditional curse of a חכם comes true
steps.raayaSupportSource: עלי's conditional curse on שמואל (שמואל א 3:17)

steps.title: שמואל kept the condition, yet his sons did not follow his ways
steps.stepSummary: Even though שמואל hid nothing from עלי, his sons later did not follow his ways, so the conditional curse still had an effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though it is written that שמואל told עלי everything and hid nothing, it is still written: 'And his sons did not walk in his ways.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. שמואל kept the condition completely, yet something bad still came upon him: his sons did not follow his path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says plainly that שמואל hid nothing, so the condition of the curse was never broken. Yet years later his sons went astray, just like עלי's sons. This shows that even a conditional curse of a חכם has an effect, which proves רבי אבהו's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: And even though
And even so
And his sons did not walk in his ways

steps.whatToRemember: Two teachings stand side by side. רב: a חכם's curse works even when it is baseless (דוד and אחיתופל). רבי אבהו: it works even when it was conditional and the condition was kept (עלי and שמואל).
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with Steps 29-32, this shows how seriously a חכם's words are taken. Even a curse that should not have taken effect still leaves a mark.

phrases.english: And even though it is written:
"And Shmuel told him all the matters,"
"and did not hide anything from him,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 3:18

phrases.english: [even so,] it is written:
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: "And his sons did not walk in his ways, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 8:3. These are שמואל's own sons, which is the curse coming true.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 34 by showing that the curse took effect even though the condition was kept
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's rule that a conditional curse of a חכם comes true
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 3:18 (שמואל hid nothing) together with שמואל א 8:3 (his sons did not follow his ways)
